2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal are that present Respondent Nos.1-11 as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No.73 of 1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Betagi, Barguna, impleading the present petitioners and others as defendants for partition of the suit land, contending inter-alia, that 7 acres of land of C.S. Khatian No.559 of Mouja-Talusi Baria, Thana and District Barguna originally belonged to Someruddin and Sher Ali in equal share; The arrear of rent of the aforesaid land was due as such Rent Suit No.229 of 1948 was instituted and the same was decreed; Execution Case No.226 of 1949 was filed and the land was put in auction on 12.07.1949; One Arshed Ali purchased the said land in auction who sold 6.88 acres of land to Haji Hachonuddin Talukder, Tajem Ali and Sekander Ali by a registered sale deed on 27.02.1951 and handed over possession thereto; Rest 12 decimals of land was in possession of Arshed Ali who died leaving one son Mohammad Ali and one daughter Dholai Bibi; Haji Hachaonuddin Talukder sold 86 decimals of land under R.S. Khatian No.54 by a registered sale deed to Samertoban Bibi on 27.03.1954; Mohabbat Ali Kha died leaving 3 sons and one daughter namely Joynal Kha, Plaintiff No.6 Salim Kha, Defendant No.41 Sohrab Kha and Piyara Begum; Said Piyara Begum died leaving husband Defendant No.3 Kanchon Ali Kha and son Defendant No.5 Belal; One Kashem Ali Kha took settlement of 65 decimals land from purchaser Haji Hachonuddin Talukder on 22.12.1952; Kashem Ali Kha sold the land on 05.11.1955 to Hatem Ali, Yousuf Ali and Hochen Ali by a registered sale deed and they sold 38 decimals of land to Tajem Ali and Sekander Ali by a registered sale deed; Hatem Ali sold 49 decimals of land under S.A. Khatian No.955 on 29.09.1951 to Mominuddin Kha, Entajuddin Kha and Afezuddin Kha; Entajuddin Kha, Mofez Kha, Rahima Bibi, Ambia and Halima Khatun sold 49 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 to Zulmat Kha on 30.04.1975; Defendant No.41 Sohrab Kha sold 13 decimals of land to Plaintiff No.2 Moslem Ali Kha who again sold the same to Defendant No.3 Kanchon Ali Kha on 12.05.1979; Haji Hachonuddin Talukder sold 6 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 to the predecessor of the plaintiff Mohabbat Ali Kha, Atahar Ali Kha, Amina Khatun and Samertaban Bibi on 27.03.1954; Haji macnonuaain Talukder died leaving two sons Defendant No.53 Hatem Ali, Yousuf Ali and 5 daughters Poribanu, Kodbanu, Iful Bibi, Rupshon Bibi and Rizia Khatun and wife Defendant No.50 Joynab Bibi; Rupshon Bibi died leaving one son Mohammad Ali and one daughter Dholai Bibi; Mohammad Ali and Dholai Bibi jointly inherited 12 decimals of land from their father and 24 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 from mother and jointly sold the same i.e. 36 decimals of land to Plaintiff Nos.2/5/6 on 24.03.1985; Atahar Ali Kha died leaving Plaintiff Nos.8-10 as heirs; Plaintiff Nos.9 and 10 sold 31 decimals of land to the Plaintiff Nos.2 and 12; Samertoban Bibi sold her entire share to Plaintiff Nos.3 and 4; Son of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder i.e. Yousuf Ali sold 1.19 acres of land to Defendant No.36 Yousuf Ali Munshi, Nurali and Abdur Razzak on 02.10.1963; Against the said transfer Mohabbat Ali Kha, Amina Khatun, Arabia Khatun and Atahar Ali Kha filed Preemption Case No.136/1964 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and obtained order of preemption on 19.11.1965 from the 1st Munsif Court of Patuakhali; Yousuf Ali died leaving mother Defendant No.50 Joynab Bibi, two wives Defendant Nos.] and 51 Maleka Begum and Kulsum Bibi respectively, one son Defendant No.49 Abdus Sobhan and one daughter Defendant No.52 Farida Begum; Hatem Ali son of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder sold 65 decimals of land to Danesh Ali and Moslem Ali Kha on 08.11.1955; Against the said transfer father of Plaintiff No.6 Mohabbat Ali Kha, Atahar Ali Kha, Amina Khatun, Art bia Khatun and Samertoban Bibi filed Pre-emption Case No.164/1959 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and obtained order of pre-emption on 23.01.1960 in which Plaintiff Nos.6-8 jointly got 45 decimals of land; Purchaser Sekander Ali died leaving son Adorn Ali, two daughter Hajera Begun, Anowara Khatun Piyara and wife Ayshon Bibi; Purchaser Tajem Ali died leaving one daughter Minara Begum, wife Maleka Begum, consanguine brother's son Adorn Ali and consanguine sister Sorbanu; Said Adorn Ali, Sorbanu, Ayesha Bibi, Hajera Bibi, Anowara Khatun and Minara Khatun sold 38 decimals of land to Plaintiff No.2 Moslem Ali Kha on 19.03.1973; Plaintiff No.2 Moslem Ali Kha transferred 10¾ of land to Defendant No.13 Shajahan; Plaintiff No.1 purchased 49½ decimals of land on 19.02.1982 and Plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 jointly purchased 80+22+42-144 decimals of land on 03.02.1985, 01.08.1987 and 02.03.1987 respectively; In this way plaintiffs' became owner and possessor of 4.41¼ of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 and 1.39 acres of land of S.A. Khatian No.954, in total 5.80¼ acres of land; Inspite of repeated requests of the plain-tiffs', the defendants refused to make amicable partition of the suit land which con-strained to file the suit for partition since there is no earlier partition by metes and bounds. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 3/5/14 and 19 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending interalia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, barred by the law of limitation and also for defect of parties; Their further case is that the suit land originally belonged to Someruddin and Sher Ali in equal share; Sher Ali died leaving two sons Osman Ali and Abdul Ali; Kashem Ali obtained 1.29 acres of land of Plot No.960 from Osman Ali and Abdul Ali on 05.05.1942 through pattan and Osman Ali received rent from Kashem Ali for the years 1349-1352 B.S. admitting Kashem Ali as an under rayat of Osman Ali who executed and registered dakhila on 16.04.1946; Sahed Ali pur-chased Marsha right from Osman Ali and Abdul Ali on 27.02.1946; Sahed Ali gave pattan through unregistered dakhila to Kashem Ali on 11.11.1946 and the said pattan was made during revisional survey and for that reason R.S. and S.A. Khatians were not published in the name of Kashem Ali; Though the land.was not recorded in S.A. Khatian in the name of Kashem Ali but he had been owning and possessing said land through pattan; Sahed Ali and Abdul Ali transferred 1.42 acres of land of Khatian No.955 on 05.11.1955 to Hatem Ali, Yousuf Ali, Hochen Ali and Kashem Ali; By virtue of the said deed Kashem Ali acquired 35½ of land; Kashem Ali being the owner of 1.64½ of land by way of pattan and kabala executed registered will infavour of his two sons and others i.e. Defendant Nos.3/14 Dholu Kha and Asmot Ali; Said Dholu Kha died leaving wife Nurjahan Begum, son Delowar Hossain and 3 daughters namely Rahima, Halima and Reba; Kashem Ali took pattan of 65 decimals of land trom Haji Hachonuddin Talukder on 22.12.1952 from C.S. Khatian No.410 and subsequently transferred the said land to Kobbat. Ali; Sobder, Sadar, Hachon Uddin and Hochon Uddin were owners and possessor of the land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.545 in equal share; Sobder Ali died leaving two sons and 3 daughters namely Arshed Ali, Kodom Ali, Borujan, Mayajan and Dwitiya Bibi where each son got 1.01 acres of land and each daughter got 50½ of land; Sadar Ali died leaving his mother Meherjan and two cousin Arshed Ali and Kodom Ali as heirs and they sold their 4 annas share to Haji Hachonuddin Talukder, Ketab Ali, Ahad Ali and Arena Bibi on 25.04.1941; Arshed Ali died leaving two sons Ketab Ali and Akkel Ali; Akkel Ali died leaving his full brother Ketab Ali as heirs; Ketab Ali (son of Arshed Ali) transferred his land to Ketab Ali (son of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder) on 12.03.1940 through pattan and gave dakhila admitting him as under tenant and in the said pattan the share of Borujan and Mayajan was not included; Dwitiya Bibi transferred 50½ decimals of land to Haji Hachonuddin Talukder; Again Borujan Bibi transferred 50½ decimals of land to Haji Hachonuddin Talukder on 21.10.1953; In this way Haji Hachonuddin Talukder obtained 5.54 acres of land amongst which 4.58½ acres of land was his recorded land and he transferred 1.89½ acres of land to Azahar Ali and Paribanu; Said Paribanu sold her portion of land to the defendants on 19.07.1979; Rest land of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder was put in auction and Sirajuddin and others purchased 4.86 acres of land in that auction; Against the said auction Yousuf Ali filed Case No.38/1967 in the 1st Munsif Court of Patuakhali to set-aside the auction. In the said case the auction purchaser amicably released 90 decimals of land infavour of Yousuf Ali; On the death of Yousuf Ali this defendants inherited said 90 decimals of land; Ketab Ali son of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder acquired 1.90 acres of land by way of pattan and kabala and thereafter died leaving wife Borujan, one son Hochen and father Haji Hachonuddin Talukder as heirs; Said Hochen Ali died leaving wife Rejia and two consanguine paternal uncle Hatem Ali and Yousuf Ali; Rejia sold 23 decimals of land on 09.04.1979 to Defendant Nos.3/19 and Plaintiff No.1 jointly; Haji Hachonuddin Talukder being owner of four annas of land of C.S. Khatian No.545 died leaving wife Amina Bibi and one son Ahad Ali; Said Amina Bibi died leaving one son Ahad Ali; Said Ahad Ali being the owner of 5.32 acres of land died leaving two sons Sekander Ali and Tajem Ali; Said Tajem Ali sold 22 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.954 to Abdul Khobir on 31.03.1964; In this way the defendants acquired 7.01½ of land of S.A. Khatian No.954 by way of inheritance and purchase and have been using and possessing their portion of land peacefully; Plaintiffs' filed this suit with false and baseless claim which is liable to be dismissed. 

 19. Admittedly, the suit land appertaining to C. Khatian No.559 belonged to Someruddin and Sher Ali in equal share. Plaintiffs/respondents claimed that their predecessor got the suit land by auction purchase and subsequently plaintiffs/ respondents got the same through some registered sale deeds. On the other hand, the contested defendants/appellants denied the alleged auction purchase of the plaintiffs and also claimed that the suit is barred b defect of parties and bad for hutch-pot. Again, they claimed that their predecessor got the suit land through settlement and later on they got the same by way of deed of will as well as some registered sale deeds. 

 23. On perusal of the evidence on record it appears that P.W.-0 1 admitted in his cross-examination that the wife of Defendant No.14 i.e. Moiful Bibi and 3 sons namely Malek, Sultan and Altaf Hossain are in possession of the suit land. Thus, from such admission it is crystal clear that the fact of possessing a portion of suit land by the Moiful Babi, Malek, Sultan and Altaf Hossain is in the knowledge of the plaintiffs, as such it was the duty of the plaintiffs/ respondents to implead them as parties to avoid multiplicity of proceedings. But on perusal of plaint it appears that the above mentioned four persons are not made parties to the suit, Again, according to the plaint, the land of C.S. Khatian No.559 is subsequently recorded in R.S. Khatian Nos.54,55,607 and S.A. Khatian Nos.418,954,955,951/1, 911 respectively. But on scrutiny of the plaint it appears that the plaintiffs/ respondents did not give any description about the names of individuals in whose names R.S. and S.A. Khatians were recorded. So, in the absence of such description it is not possible to ascertain whether all the R.S. and S.A. tenants are made parties to the suit. 

 27. On perusal of record it appears that P. -01 admitted in his cross-examination that he doesn't know how much land there is in the former (sabek) plots and how much lands of the former (sabek) plots has been recorded in current (hal) plots. Again, the appellate court below on perusal of exhibit-2 and 2 (lea) arrived at a finding that the former (sabek) plot numbers of the current (hal) Plot Nos.2282 and 2285 are 96 and 909 respectively. The appellate court below also arrived at a finding that in the said exhibited docu-ment no former (sabek) plot number of current Plot No. 2284/2935 is mentioned. On perusal of plaint 2935 and exhibit-01 i.e. C.S. Khatian No.559 it appears that former Plot Nos.96 and 909 are not included in the schedule of the plaint as well as in the C.S. Khatian No.559. In this context appellate court below upon evidences on record arrived at a conclusive finding that the suit is barred by hutch-pot for non-inclusion of the land of former (sabek) Plot Nos.96 and 909 in the schedule of the plaint. Inspite of such finding of the appellate court below, the High Court Division did not utter a single word to controvert such finding of the appellate court below. 

 The contesting defendants raised a dispute regarding auction sale of the suit property in Rent Suit No.229 of 1948 and Rent Decree Execution Case No.226 of 1949 and stated that the land of C.S. Khatian No.559 was not sold in auction. It has been clearly stated that the land in Sabek Khabot No.410 has been subsequently recorded in C.S. Khatian No.559 and the land of said Khabot No.410 corresponding to C.S. Khatian No.559 was sold in auction." 

 34. Plaintiffs/respondents claimed that their predecessor purchased the suit land through auction. The plaintiffs filed the suit for partition of C.S. Khatian No.559 and claimed that the land mentioned in C.S. Khatian No,559 and Khabot Khatian No.410 are same and on perusal on exhib-it-06 i.e. sale certificate of land in Rent Suit no. 229 of 1948 it appears that the same do not contain any C.S. Khatian number, rather contain only Khabot Khatian No.410, so it was the duty of the plaintiffs/respondents to establish such claim through relay of the land of C.S. Khatian No.559 with that of Khabot Khatian No.410 by appointing a survey knowing advocate commissioner. But on perusal of record it appears that the plaintiffs/ respondents did not take any such initiatives to establish their claim. Moreover, on perusal of exhibit-06 it appears that Arshed Ali purchased 7 acres of land in that auction. Again, exhibit-06 stated that Arshed Ali purchased the land corresponding to Khabot Khatian No.410 which is under annual rent of 51 taka 9 annas. On perusal of exhibit-1 i.e. C.S. Khatian No it appears that the entire 7 acres of land of that khatian is under annual rent of 64 taka. It is to be mentioned here that if the land of Khabot Khatian No.410 and C.S. Khatian No.559 are same then the annual rent of two khatians should be the same, but in reality the annual rent of both the khatians are not same. Thus, from the above discussions it appears to us that the plaintiff failed to prove that their predecessor purchased the land of C.S. Khatian No.559 through auction, as such the claim of auction purchase of the land of C.S. Khatian No. 559 by the plaintiffs is not proved.
